Why split. The supplied 10-step proof combines four independent obligations of different kinds. Each is a self-contained, reusable statement.
- finite_measure (step 2): Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for every integer multiplicity triple and compact K ⊆ U. This is the standard local finiteness of Hⁿ⌞M, and it makes μ_K a finite measure. It is reusable wherever τ(M, θ, ξ) with integer θ must be localized, e.g. the hypothesis "∀ K compact, μHE[m](A ∩ K) < ∞" of the interval_product children.
- unit_bound (step 4): |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ when ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector of an orthonormal frame. This is exactly the accepted fiw_ims_tt_unit_bound, so it is reused, not re-proved.
- nvector_integral (step 8): an n-vector commutes with the pointwise interval integral of a continuous covector family. This applies to any form defined by a pointwise s-integral, such as the radial operator ψ(x)(v) = ∫ t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt of the cone construction.
- param_fubini (steps 5, 6 and 8): ∫_0^1 ∫ θ ξ(Φ(s)) dμ ds = ∫ θ ξ(Ψ) dμ. It assumes an s-finite μ, an integrable θ, a ξ with a.e. unit bound, a jointly continuous Φ bounded on [0, 1] × ℝ^P, and Ψ the pointwise s-integral of Φ. This is the analytic core: a dominated Fubini exchange that does not mention currents. It uses nvector_integral.

subproblems.title: Integer multiplicity triples have locally finite Hⁿ-measure: Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, M, K ⊆ ℝ^P, θ : ℝ^P → ℝ and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (NVector (Eucl P) n). Assume IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ (frozen contract): M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, θ > 0 on M, θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K' for every compact K' ⊆ U, plus the measurability and orientation fields. Assume also that θ is integer-valued on M (for every x ∈ M there is k ∈ ℕ with θ(x) = k), that K is compact and that K ⊆ U. Then Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞, where Hⁿ = μHE[n] is the Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (K : Set (Eucl P)), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ x ∈ M, ∃ k : ℕ, θ x = k) → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M ∩ K) < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 1–2 of the parent proof of iwl_cr_ci_integral_exchange. Those steps show θ ≥ 1 on M and then μ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} |θ| dHᵐ < ∞. Here they are stated for an arbitrary domain U and an arbitrary compact K ⊆ U, with details filled in.

Notation: E := ℝ^P = Eucl P and μ := μHE[n], the Hausdorff measure Hⁿ on E. For real r, ‖r‖ₑ = ENNReal.ofReal |r| (Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs). The hypotheses are IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ (frozen contract), the integer property ∀ x ∈ M, ∃ k : ℕ, θ x = k, IsCompact K and K ⊆ U. The proof uses only three fields of IsRectifiableTriple:
- nullMeasurableSet: M is μ-null-measurable;
- pos: θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M;
- integrableOn: θ is μ-integrable on M ∩ K' for every compact K' ⊆ U.

1. (θ ≥ 1 on M.) Let x ∈ M. By hypothesis θ(x) = k for some k ∈ ℕ, and by `pos`, 0 < θ(x) = k. If k = 0 then θ(x) = 0, which is impossible. So k ≥ 1 (Nat.one_le_iff_ne_zero) and θ(x) = k ≥ 1 (cast to ℝ).
2. (Integrability.) K is compact and K ⊆ U, so `integrableOn` gives IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μ, i.e. θ is integrable for μ.restrict (M ∩ K). In particular its integral is finite (Integrable.hasFiniteIntegral): ∫⁻ ‖θ‖ₑ d(μ.restrict (M ∩ K)) < ∞.
3. (Null-measurability.) M is μ-null-measurable. K is compact in the Hausdorff space E, hence closed, hence Borel measurable. So M ∩ K is μ-null-measurable (NullMeasurableSet.inter), and μ.restrict (M ∩ K)-a.e. x lies in M ∩ K (ae_restrict_mem₀).
4. (A.e. lower bound.) For μ.restrict (M ∩ K)-a.e. x we have x ∈ M by step 3, so θ(x) ≥ 1 by step 1. Then |θ(x)| = θ(x) ≥ 1, so ‖θ(x)‖ₑ = ENNReal.ofReal |θ(x)| ≥ 1 (ENNReal.one_le_ofReal).
5. (Conclusion.) The lower integral of the constant 1 for μ.restrict (M ∩ K) equals μ(M ∩ K). Therefore μ(M ∩ K) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} 1 dμ ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩K} ‖θ‖ₑ dμ < ∞. The inequality is lintegral_mono_ae with step 4, and the strict bound is step 2. ∎

θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K (field integrableOn, K compact ⊆ U), and M ∩ K is Hⁿ-null-measurable, so Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K)-a.e. x lies in M and has ‖θ(x)‖ₑ ≥ 1.

subproblems.title: Operator-norm unit bound for ± simple n-vectors of orthonormal frames
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) : Fin n → ℝ^P be an orthonormal family. Let w ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (NVector (Eucl P) n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) satisfy w = simpleNVector τ or w = −simpleNVector τ. Then |w(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every n-covector α (Covector (Eucl P) n: a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ, with its operator norm ‖α‖).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P) (w : NVector (Eucl P) n), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (w = simpleNVector τ ∨ w = -simpleNVector τ) → ∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) n, |w α| ≤ ‖α‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Provenance (reused child). This child is the existing comparator-accepted declaration `Submission.fiw_ims_tt_unit_bound`. Its DAG node is root.flat_iff_weak-a1.im_series-a1.tsum_tau-a1.unit_bound-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 27af9b191b732eae73e3d693d8903e52f89962ce, comparator_passed true). Its title, statement and frozen Lean type are copied byte-for-byte from dag.json, and it depends on no sibling. The runtime therefore maps this key to that node and creates no new node. Other decompositions reuse it the same way, for example root.boundary_rectifiability-a1.localization-a1. The numbered proof below is that node's accepted parent-supplied natural proof, copied verbatim. Its Lean proof is already comparator-accepted, so this split re-proves nothing.

Role in iwl_cr_ci_integral_exchange: step 4 (second half) of the supplied proof. Applied inside the field `orients`, it gives |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every m-covector α, for μHE[m].restrict M-a.e. x. The parent restricts this to μ_K = μHE[m].restrict (M ∩ K) and passes it to the sibling param_fubini as its a.e. orientation bound.

--- Verbatim accepted proof ---

Notation: s(τ) := simpleNVector τ. For an n-covector α (a continuous alternating map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ), ‖α‖ is its operator norm.

1. (Unit vectors.) Since τ is orthonormal, ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i ∈ Fin n (first component of Orthonormal). Hence ∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = 1; for n = 0 the empty product is also 1.
2. (Evaluation.) By the definition of simpleNVector (simpleNVector_apply), s(τ)(α) = α(τ) = α(τ_1, …, τ_n).
3. (Operator-norm inequality.) For continuous alternating maps, ‖α(τ)‖ ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). By step 1 the right side equals ‖α‖. The norm on ℝ is the absolute value (Real.norm_eq_abs), so steps 2–3 give |s(τ)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
4. (Case w = s(τ).) Then |w(α)| = |s(τ)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ by step 3.
5. (Case w = −s(τ).) Evaluating a negated continuous linear map negates the value, so w(α) = −(s(τ)(α)). Hence |w(α)| = |s(τ)(α)| (abs_neg) ≤ ‖α‖ by step 3.
6. The hypothesis gives one of the cases 4 or 5, so |w(α)| ≤ ‖α‖. ∎

- `have h1 : |simpleNVector τ α| ≤ ‖α‖ := by rw [simpleNVector_apply, ← Real.norm_eq_abs]; calc ‖α τ‖ ≤ ‖α‖ * ∏ i, ‖τ i‖ := α.le_opNorm τ; _ = ‖α‖ := by simp [hτ.1]`
- then `rcases hw with rfl | rfl`, with `exact h1` and `simpa [abs_neg] using h1`.
- Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: the case w = −simpleNVector τ reduces to the same bound by |−a| = |a|

subproblems.title: An n-vector commutes with the pointwise interval integral of a continuous covector family
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and a, b ∈ ℝ. Let f : ℝ → Λ^m(ℝ^P) be continuous, where Λ^m(ℝ^P) = Covector (Eucl P) m is the space of continuous alternating m-linear maps (ℝ^P)^m → ℝ with the operator norm. Let c ∈ Λ^m(ℝ^P) satisfy c(v) = ∫_a^b f(s)(v) ds for every v : Fin m → ℝ^P, and let w ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P) = NVector (Eucl P) m be a continuous linear functional on m-covectors. Then ∫_a^b w(f(s)) ds = w(c). Integrals are interval integrals for Lebesgue measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (a b : ℝ) (f : ℝ → Covector (Eucl P) m) (c : Covector (Eucl P) m) (w : NVector (Eucl P) m), Continuous f → (∀ v : Fin m → Eucl P, c v = ∫ s in a..b, f s v) → ∫ s in a..b, w (f s) = w c
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 8 of the parent proof of iwl_cr_ci_integral_exchange. That step identifies ∫ φ(s)(x) ds with ψ(x) through evaluation functionals, then moves the continuous linear functional ξ(x) inside the s-integral. Here it is stated for a general interval and a general continuous family of covectors, with details filled in.

Notation: Λ^m := Covector (Eucl P) m = (ℝ^P)[⋀^Fin m]→L[ℝ] ℝ with the operator norm. NVector (Eucl P) m = Λ^m →L[ℝ] ℝ. All integrals ∫_a^b are interval integrals for Lebesgue measure.

1. (The Bochner integral exists.) Λ^m is a complete normed space (ContinuousAlternatingMap.instCompleteSpace, since ℝ is complete). f is continuous, so it is interval integrable on [a, b] (Continuous.intervalIntegrable). Hence I := ∫_a^b f(s) ds ∈ Λ^m is the genuine Bochner interval integral.
2. (Evaluation functionals.) Fix v : Fin m → ℝ^P and define L_v : Λ^m → ℝ by L_v(α) := α(v). L_v is continuous linear: it is ContinuousMultilinearMap.apply ℝ (fun _ => ℝ^P) ℝ v composed with the continuous linear map ContinuousAlternatingMap.toContinuousMultilinearMapCLM ℝ. The identity L_v(α) = α(v) holds definitionally.
3. (Continuous linear maps commute with interval integrals.) Let L : G →L[ℝ] H with G, H complete normed spaces, and let g be interval integrable. Then ∫_a^b L(g(s)) ds = L(∫_a^b g(s) ds) (ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm).
4. (I = c.) For each v, step 3 with L = L_v and g = f gives I(v) = L_v(I) = ∫_a^b L_v(f(s)) ds = ∫_a^b f(s)(v) ds. By hypothesis the last integral is c(v). Two continuous alternating maps that agree at every v are equal (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext), so I = c.
5. (Conclusion.) w is a continuous linear functional on the complete space Λ^m. Step 3 with L = w and g = f, then step 4, gives ∫_a^b w(f(s)) ds = w(∫_a^b f(s) ds) = w(I) = w(c). ∎

        (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toContinuousMultilinearMapCLM ℝ)
    have hL : ∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) m, L α = α v := fun α => rfl
    have h := L.intervalIntegral_comp_comm hfi
    simp only [hL] at h
    exact h.symm
  rw [w.intervalIntegral_comp_comm hfi, hI]
```
proof_key_steps: f is continuous, hence interval integrable, and Covector (Eucl P) m is complete, so I := ∫_a^b f(s) ds exists.
Evaluation at v is a continuous linear functional and commutes with the interval integral: I(v) = ∫_a^b f(s)(v) ds = c(v) for all v, so I = c (ContinuousAlternatingMap.ext).
w commutes with the interval integral: ∫_a^b w(f(s)) ds = w(I) = w(c) (ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm).

subproblems.title: Parametric Fubini for the τ-integrand: ∫_0^1 ∫ θ ξ(Φ(s)) dμ ds = ∫ θ ξ(Ψ) dμ
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, B ∈ ℝ and let μ be an s-finite measure on ℝ^P. Let θ : ℝ^P → ℝ be μ-integrable. Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P) (NVector (Eucl P) m) be μ-AEStronglyMeasurable, with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every m-covector α, for μ-a.e. x. Let Φ : ℝ → ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P) (Covector (Eucl P) m) be such that (s, x) ↦ Φ(s)(x) is continuous on ℝ × ℝ^P and ‖Φ(s)(x)‖ ≤ B for all s ∈ [0, 1] and x ∈ ℝ^P. Let Ψ : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P) satisfy Ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 Φ(s)(x)(v) ds for all x ∈ ℝ^P and v : Fin m → ℝ^P. Then ∫_0^1 (∫ θ(x) ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)) dμ(x)) ds = ∫ θ(x) ξ(x)(Ψ(x)) dμ(x).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) m) (Φ : ℝ → Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) m) (Ψ : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) m) (B : ℝ), SFinite μ → Integrable θ μ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) m, |ξ x α| ≤ ‖α‖) → Continuous (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => Φ p.1 p.2) → (∀ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x, ‖Φ s x‖ ≤ B) → (∀ (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin m → Eucl P), Ψ x v = ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..1, Φ s x v) → ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..1, ∫ x, θ x * ξ x (Φ s x) ∂μ = ∫ x, θ x * ξ x (Ψ x) ∂μ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 5, 6 and 8 of the parent proof of iwl_cr_ci_integral_exchange (integrability on the product, Fubini, the inner s-integral), together with the domination estimate of its step 4. Two things are abstracted:
- the localized finite measure μ_K becomes an arbitrary s-finite measure μ;
- the slice family φ becomes an arbitrary jointly continuous family Φ that is uniformly bounded by B on [0, 1] × ℝ^P.
Details are filled in. The proof uses the sibling nvector_integral (Submission.iwl_cr_ci_ie_nvector_intervalIntegral).

Notation:
- E := ℝ^P and Λ^m := Covector E m with the operator norm;
- ν := volume.restrict (Ioc 0 1), Lebesgue measure on (0, 1];
- F(s, x) := θ(x) · ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)) for (s, x) ∈ ℝ × E, viewed as the uncurried function of the curried F s x;
- ∫_0^1 denotes the interval integral for Lebesgue measure.

1. (The factor measures.) ν(ℝ) = vol(Ioc 0 1) = 1 < ∞, so ν is finite and hence s-finite. μ is s-finite by hypothesis. So the product measure ν.prod μ on ℝ × E is available, together with the Fubini lemmas for s-finite factors.
2. (F is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν.prod μ.)
   (a) θ is μ-integrable, hence μ-AEStronglyMeasurable. So (s, x) ↦ θ(x) is ν.prod μ-AEStronglyMeasurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_snd, using SFinite μ).
   (b) In the same way, (s, x) ↦ ξ(x) is ν.prod μ-AEStronglyMeasurable.
   (c) (s, x) ↦ Φ(s)(x) is continuous on ℝ × E. That space is second countable with its Borel σ-algebra, and Λ^m is a metric space, so the map is AEStronglyMeasurable (Continuous.aestronglyMeasurable).
   (d) The evaluation (w, α) ↦ w(α) on NVector E m × Λ^m is continuous (continuous_fst.clm_apply continuous_snd). Hence (s, x) ↦ ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)) is AEStronglyMeasurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ applied to (b) and (c)).
   (e) F is the product of (a) and (d), so it is AEStronglyMeasurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul).
3. (Integrable majorant.) Let G(s, x) := B · |θ(x)|.
   - The constant B is ν-integrable (integrable_const, since ν is finite).
   - |θ| = ‖θ‖ is μ-integrable (Integrable.norm).
   So G is ν.prod μ-integrable (Integrable.mul_prod, using SFinite μ).
4. (Domination a.e.)
   - ν-a.e. s lies in Ioc 0 1 (ae_restrict_mem; Ioc 0 1 is measurable).
   - By hypothesis, μ-a.e. x satisfies |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every α ∈ Λ^m.
   Prod.fst : (ℝ × E, ν.prod μ) → (ℝ, ν) and Prod.snd : (ℝ × E, ν.prod μ) → (E, μ) are quasi-measure-preserving (Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_fst / _snd). So both properties hold for ν.prod μ-a.e. (s, x) (QuasiMeasurePreserving.ae). Fix such an (s, x). Then s ∈ Ioc 0 1 ⊆ Icc 0 1, so ‖Φ(s)(x)‖ ≤ B by the bound hypothesis. Hence ‖F(s, x)‖ = |θ(x)| · |ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x))| ≤ |θ(x)| · ‖Φ(s)(x)‖ ≤ |θ(x)| · B = G(s, x), multiplying by |θ(x)| ≥ 0. No sign or size condition on B or θ is needed.
5. (Integrability.) Steps 2, 3 and 4 with Integrable.mono' show that F is ν.prod μ-integrable.
6. (Fubini.) By MeasureTheory.integral_integral_swap (both factors s-finite): ∫ (∫ F(s, x) dμ(x)) dν(s) = ∫ (∫ F(s, x) dν(s)) dμ(x).
7. (Left side.) Since 0 ≤ 1, ∫_0^1 g(s) ds = ∫_{Ioc 0 1} g(s) ds = ∫ g dν for every g : ℝ → ℝ (intervalIntegral.integral_of_le). With g(s) := ∫ θ(x) ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)) dμ(x), the left side of the claim is therefore the left side of step 6.
8. (Inner s-integral.) Fix x ∈ E. By integral_of_le again, ∫ F(s, x) dν(s) = ∫_0^1 θ(x) · ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)) ds. Pulling out the constant gives θ(x) · ∫_0^1 ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)) ds (intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul). The map s ↦ Φ(s)(x) is continuous: it is the jointly continuous map composed with s ↦ (s, x) (Continuous.prodMk continuous_id continuous_const). By hypothesis Ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 Φ(s)(x)(v) ds for every v. Apply the sibling nvector_integral with a = 0, b = 1, f = (s ↦ Φ(s)(x)), c = Ψ(x) and w = ξ(x). This gives ∫_0^1 ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)) ds = ξ(x)(Ψ(x)), hence ∫ F(s, x) dν(s) = θ(x) · ξ(x)(Ψ(x)).
9. (Conclusion.) Combining steps 7, 6 and 8: ∫_0^1 ∫ θ(x) ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)) dμ(x) ds = ∫ (∫ F(s, x) dν(s)) dμ(x) = ∫ θ(x) ξ(x)(Ψ(x)) dμ(x). ∎

Lean note (non-normative; kernel-checked in scratch at this pin, in the comparator scope, as `theorem Submission.iwl_cr_ci_ie_param_fubini : <frozen type> := by …`, after the sibling; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
```
  intro P m μ θ ξ Φ Ψ B hμ hθ hξ hbd hΦ hB hΨ
  set ν : Measure ℝ := volume.restrict (Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1) with hν
  have _instν : IsFiniteMeasure ν := ⟨by simp [hν]⟩
  set F : ℝ → Eucl P → ℝ := fun s x => θ x * ξ x (Φ s x) with hF
  have hmeas : AEStronglyMeasurable (Function.uncurry F) (ν.prod μ) := by
    have h1 : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => θ p.2) (ν.prod μ) :=
      hθ.aestronglyMeasurable.comp_snd
    have h2 : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => ξ p.2) (ν.prod μ) := hξ.comp_snd
    have h3 : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => Φ p.1 p.2) (ν.prod μ) :=
      hΦ.aestronglyMeasurable
    have h4 : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => ξ p.2 (Φ p.1 p.2)) (ν.prod μ) :=
      (continuous_fst.clm_apply continuous_snd).comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂ h2 h3
    exact h1.mul h4
  have hG : Integrable (fun p : ℝ × Eucl P => B * ‖θ p.2‖) (ν.prod μ) :=
    (integrable_const B).mul_prod hθ.norm
  have hbound : ∀ᵐ p ∂(ν.prod μ), ‖Function.uncurry F p‖ ≤ B * ‖θ p.2‖ := by
    have hs : ∀ᵐ p ∂(ν.prod μ), p.1 ∈ Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1 :=
      Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_fst.ae (ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Ioc)
    have hx : ∀ᵐ p ∂(ν.prod μ), ∀ α : Covector (Eucl P) m, |ξ p.2 α| ≤ ‖α‖ :=
      Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_snd.ae hbd
    filter_upwards [hs, hx] with p hp1 hp2
    simp only [Function.uncurry, hF, norm_mul, Real.norm_eq_abs]
    calc |θ p.2| * |ξ p.2 (Φ p.1 p.2)| ≤ |θ p.2| * B := by
          gcongr
          exact (hp2 _).trans (hB p.1 (Ioc_subset_Icc_self hp1) p.2)
      _ = B * |θ p.2| := mul_comm _ _
  have hint : Integrable (Function.uncurry F) (ν.prod μ) := hG.mono' hmeas hbound
  have hswap := integral_integral_swap hint
  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_of_le zero_le_one]
  change ∫ s, ∫ x, F s x ∂μ ∂ν = _
  rw [hswap]
  congr 1
  funext x
  change ∫ s in Ioc (0 : ℝ) 1, θ x * ξ x (Φ s x) = _
  rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le zero_le_one, intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul]
  congr 1
  exact Submission.iwl_cr_ci_ie_nvector_intervalIntegral P m 0 1 (fun s => Φ s x) (Ψ x) (ξ x)

proof_key_steps: Put ν := Lebesgue⌞(0, 1] (finite) and F(s, x) := θ(x) ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)). F is AEStronglyMeasurable on ν ⊗ μ (comp_snd for θ and ξ, continuity of Φ, continuous evaluation).
ν ⊗ μ-a.e., s ∈ (0, 1] and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖, so |F(s, x)| ≤ B |θ(x)|. B|θ| is ν ⊗ μ-integrable (Integrable.mul_prod), so F is integrable (Integrable.mono').
Fubini (integral_integral_swap) exchanges ∫ dν and ∫ dμ; ∫_0^1 = ∫ dν by intervalIntegral.integral_of_le.
The inner integral is θ(x) ∫_0^1 ξ(x)(Φ(s)(x)) ds = θ(x) ξ(x)(Ψ(x)) by nvector_integral.
